correctness.rationale: The inverse output-labeled predecessor maps directly prove the necessary-and-sufficient invariant-subset normal form. Choosing its fixed set produces the exact flat labeled count. Burnside centralizers plus the invariant-subset identity prove the partition orbit polynomial. Labeled exponential decomposition and unlabeled multiset Möbius inversion prove the connected enumerators. An explicit first-and-second moment argument for simultaneously invariant state subsets proves the 1-2/n+O(n^-2) connected proportion. The actual packaged standard-library verifier directly enumerates all n<=5 machines, canonicalizes state-only classes for n<=4, independently tests the GAP state+alphabet quotient at n=2, and checks formal coefficients to n=10 or 12. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The precisely delimited new theorem is an all-positive-n labeled count refined by output-swap size, an all-n state-only-isomorphism Burnside polynomial, two connected-component enumerators, and a connectivity asymptotic. The motivating 2026 structural source establishes Latin-like and isotopism frameworks in accessible material, not these exact formulas. Woryna studies generated groups for two states, Godin–Klimann studies connected reversible automata and Burnside-group properties, and the GAP FR package records only small machine counts with alphabet relabeling also permitted. The GAP two-state labeled count of twelve corroborates rather than covers the all-length claim. Multiple searched exact-number sequences, aliases and automaton-normal-form descriptions yielded no direct covering statement. The inaccessible 57-page 2026 full primary paper is an explicit nontrivial residual priority risk, but no affirmative covering theorem was identified in accessible evidence.

value.rationale: Bireversible Mealy machines are a natural class whose connected components underpin automaton-group investigations, and Curtin–Savchuk explicitly motivates combinatorial encoding and isotopy questions. The theorem determines an unknown exact all-n isomorphism-class polynomial for this fixed alphabet, exact connected refinements and a quantitative connected fraction; its non-obvious invariant-subset normal form makes Burnside and multiset enumeration workable. These benchmark quantities are natural, complete parameter families, not an arbitrary finite cutoff or a simple substitution of a published table. The broad scope and independent small-machine corroboration support future enumeration and classification applications without claiming any group-theoretic consequence not proved.
